name: Chest Dip
description: The chest dip is a compound bodyweight or weighted pushing exercise performed on parallel bars with a forward torso lean. By inclining the torso forward, the lower and outer pectoral muscles are emphasized over the triceps, making it an effective mass-building exercise for the lower chest.

execution.starting_position: Support yourself on parallel dip bars with arms extended. Lean your torso forward at approximately 30 degrees by crossing your feet behind and allowing your hips to tilt forward.
execution.setup_instructions: Set dip bar width to slightly wider than shoulder width. The forward lean is what distinguishes a chest dip from a tricep dip — without it, the triceps dominate.
steps: With the forward lean maintained, lower yourself by bending the elbows, allowing them to flare slightly outward.
Descend until shoulders are at the same height as the elbows or slightly below.
Press back up to the starting position, maintaining the forward lean throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent. Exhale on the press up.
common_mistakes: Maintaining an upright torso, shifting emphasis to the triceps instead of the chest
Dipping below the shoulder level of safe range, stressing the anterior shoulder capsule
Allowing the elbows to flare excessively wide
safety_considerations: Stop the descent when shoulders begin to feel uncomfortable — this varies by individual
Individuals with shoulder impingement or anterior shoulder pain should approach with caution
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Upper arms reach parallel or slightly below parallel to the floor at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Lean forward — the more you lean, the more chest you use
Think about pushing the bars behind you rather than pressing straight down
